claim: RZ-NAS (Ji, Zhu, Yuan, Huang; ICML 2025) is a confirmed, officially published counter-example in which LLM-generated reflective feedback embedded in an iterative evolutionary search loop achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple NAS benchmarks and downstream tasks, contradicting a blanket claim that LLM feedback always degrades architecture search.
stance_target: iterative LLM feedback always degrades rather than improves architecture search proposals
scope_conditions: ICML 2025 (42nd ICML), micro and macro NAS search spaces, multiple standard NAS benchmarks and downstream tasks
quoted_support: By integrating LLM reflection modules, we use LLM-generated feedback to provide linguistic guidance within architecture optimization. RZ-NAS enables effective search within both micro and macro search spaces without extensive time cost, achieving SOTA performance across multiple downstream tasks.

claim: RZ-NAS's reflective feedback loop scores mutations with zero-cost (training-free) proxy metrics rather than full trained accuracy, and operates within an evolutionary mutation-selection pipeline that can discard a bad LLM-suggested mutation -- structurally different from a pure sequential self-refinement setup where every LLM output must be accepted as the new baseline for the next round.
stance_target: whether RZ-NAS's positive feedback result directly contradicts or merely differs in scale/setup from a claim about sequential self-refinement degradation
scope_conditions: RZ-NAS method design, ICML 2025 poster lay summary
quoted_support: The reflective module guides the LLM to reflect on mutation performance and generates targeted suggestions for further iteration improvements.

claim: Existing LLM-to-NAS methods prior to RZ-NAS were explicitly criticized by its authors for limited search spaces, poor time-cost search efficiency, and uncompetitive performance versus standard NAS benchmarks -- an admission from within the LLM-NAS literature itself that the field's baseline LLM-guided methods often underperform.
stance_target: general competitiveness of LLM-guided NAS methods against standard baselines prior to reflective/zero-cost improvements
scope_conditions: RZ-NAS abstract framing of prior LLM-to-NAS work, ICML 2025
quoted_support: However, the existing LLM-to-NAS methods face the challenges of limited search spaces, time-cost search efficiency, and uncompetitive performance across standard NAS benchmarks and multiple downstream tasks.

claim: The base LLM's parameter scale and quantisation status are not disclosed on the RZ-NAS poster/lay-summary page, so RZ-NAS cannot be directly cited as evidence about how feedback effects vary with model scale or quantisation without consulting the full paper.
stance_target: RZ-NAS as evidence for or against a scale/quantisation-dependent feedback effect
scope_conditions: Limitation of the poster-level source; full paper PDF needed to resolve
quoted_support: the base LLM's scale/quantization is not disclosed on this page
